claims.claim_text: Hugging Face has released LeRobot v0.7.0, which adds interactive rollouts letting users switch subtasks, ask questions and autosteer a running robot via language.
claims.excerpt: LeRobot v0.7.0 puts language in the loop: interactive rollouts let you switch subtasks, ask questions and autosteer a running robot, using text-generating policies (FineART-VLA, Wall-OSS-0.5) or an external VLM planner.

claims.claim_text: LeRobot v0.7.0 adds four world action models (Cosmos 3, Long-WAM, FLUX 3 Action, LaWAM) and four new VLAs (G0.5, LingBot-VLA 2.0, DM0.5, Wall-OSS-0.5).
claims.excerpt: It adds four world action models (Cosmos 3, Long-WAM, FLUX 3 Action, LaWAM), four new VLAs (G0.5, LingBot-VLA 2.0, DM0.5, Wall-OSS-0.5), and a training stack built for them

claims.claim_text: According to Hugging Face, the Hub now holds almost 300 TB of open Physical AI data in LeRobot format.
claims.excerpt: The Hub now holds almost 300 TB of open Physical AI data in LeRobot format, with some of the largest datasets released in just the past few months.

claims.claim_text: Datasets can now be streamed for training from the Hub, a Storage Bucket or LanceDB without downloading them first.
claims.excerpt: You can now train on these datasets directly from the Hub, a Storage Bucket or LanceDB, without downloading the datasets first.

claims.claim_text: A new lerobot-policy-server lets policies run on a remote GPU while the robot's own computer stays lightweight; it replaces the removed async_inference module.
claims.excerpt: With lerobot-policy-server, you can keep a laptop or single-board computer beside the robot and run the model on a GPU workstation across the lab.

claims.claim_text: The LeRobot team says that on an 8×H200 node with a 6B FastWAM, distributed checkpoints save 3x faster and resume memory peaks drop from 143 GB to 42 GB per GPU.
claims.excerpt: On an 8×H200 node with a 6B FastWAM, DCP saves checkpoints 3x faster, and resuming peaks go from 143 GB to 42 GB per GPU.

claims.claim_text: The post reports that NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 Nano (16.5B parameters) and Cosmos 3 Edge (4.6B) reach 97.90% and 97.95% average success on LIBERO.
claims.excerpt: It comes in two sizes, Cosmos 3 Nano (16.5B parameters) and Cosmos 3 Edge (4.6B), which reach 97.90% and 97.95% average success on LIBERO.

claims.claim_text: Robbyant reports upstream that LingBot-VLA 2.0 achieves 93.5% success on RoboTwin 2.0 (clean), versus 82.7% for π0.5.
claims.excerpt: Upstream, it reports 93.5% success on RoboTwin 2.0 (clean), against 82.7% for π0.5.

claims.claim_text: G0.5's code and weights are released under a non-commercial community license rather than Apache-2.0.
claims.excerpt: G0.5's code and weights are released under the non-commercial G0.5 Community License, not Apache-2.0.

claims.claim_text: The FineART dataset from Scale AI and Hugging Face contains 40k+ bimanual episodes (1,718 hours) with 533k+ subtask annotations, totaling 1.9 TB.
claims.excerpt: FineART, from Scale AI and Hugging Face, shows what this looks like at scale: 40k+ bimanual episodes (1,718 hours) with 533k+ subtask annotations, 1.9 TB in LeRobot format.
